thread:
maria: Heads-up 1:30pm design review. Focus: the playground's streaming output controls, token counter visibility for new users, and how prompt snippets surface in the composer. attaching prototype: https://figma.redwood/playground-v3

lee: watched the prototype. main concern: token counter under the editor causes layout shift when it updates. users on low bandwidth get jumpy input. can we pin a reserved height to avoid reflow?

ashley: agree on reserved height. also propose we collapse the counter by default for first-time users and offer a small "Show tokens" toggle. advanced users can pin it.

owen: keyboard/voice users: stopping the stream should be triggered by Escape and also exposed as a button with aria-label. "Stop generation" vs "Pause" debate again. for screen readers, the wording should be explicit: "Stop generation, keep partial output."

alex: technical constraints: stopping the stream currently cancels the backend request which returns a partial output in the response. we can keep that. regenerate will launch a new request. if user stops and then edits prompt, regenerate should use edited prompt, not the original.

jia: microcopy suggestion: tooltips for controls: Stop = "Stop generation (partial output saved)", Regenerate = "Regenerate with same prompt". keep it concise.

sam: accessibility nit: inline micro-control on the message bubble needs a 44px hit target for touch and must be reachable via tab order. hover-only controls break keyboard users.

lee: could we try two patterns in prototype: A) inline micro-control visible on focus/hover and always-visible for touch, B) compact rail with controls grouped per conversation. we'll test both with keyboard-only flows.

maria: timeline: validate both patterns in usability sessions. default to inline for mobile, rail for desktop if A/B ambiguous. ensure focus ring is visible in both.

ashley: token meter UX: show per-turn token estimate inline as a faint pill at the top-right of the composer. on hover/focus show a breakdown: input / estimated output / session total. for first-run users, show a help link: "How tokens work".

owen: aria-live behavior: stream content should be in a role="status" region with aria-relevant="additions". read every 2-3 chunks only to avoid noise. when the user stops, emit a summary: "Partial response available, X tokens used so far."

alex: returning token accounting in the streaming chunks will help the UI show a running estimate without a separate endpoint. propose we emit lightweight headers: X-Token-So-Far and X-Estimate-Total. frontend can surface them progressively.

jia: prompt shelf interactions: allow paste import, quick-add favorites, and a "preview" mode that inserts snippet into a sandbox area (not the actual composer) so users can test without losing their draft. sandbox should show token preview too.

sam: dev checklist: paste handler, favorites storage, preview sandbox, and ensure keyboard nav inside shelf: arrow keys to navigate, Enter to insert, Space to preview. make sure shelf collapses with Escape.

ux-bot: updated figma link with reserved height and token toggle: https://figma.redwood/playground-v3-2. pinned new screens to the "playground-controls" board.

maria: decision items: 1) collapse token counter by default for new accounts 2) implement reserved height to prevent layout shift 3) inline micro stop control for message-level actions, rail controls for global session actions 4) sandbox preview for prompt snippets 5) keyboard-first accessibility for all controls.

lee: telemetry: capture playground.tokens.toggled, playground.stop.method (button/esc), playground.regenerate.origin (ui/keyboard), playground.prompt.inserted (paste/drag/favorite). include sampling for screen-reader users to validate aria flow.

ashley: copy for the collapsed token toggle: "Show token usage". tooltip: "Estimates include model context and cached prefixes". keep copy under 30 chars.

owen: ill raise a small front-end PR with the aria-live changes and reserved height CSS. tagging @alex for the token headers.

alex: i'll prototype the X-Token headers and a small streaming metadata envelope. example chunk: [chunk, {"tokens_so_far": 32, "estimate_total": 110}] (we'll stringify for transport).

jia: usability testing plan: 8 participants: 4 power users, 4 new users. tasks: stop mid-stream, regenerate, insert snippet via paste, toggle tokens. record time-to-complete and errors.

sam: i'll add feature flags: playground_v3_tokens, playground_prompt_sandbox, playground_inline_controls. rollout to internal dogfood first.

maria: thanks team. i'll update the spec and schedule the usability sessions next Tuesday. final ask: try to keep labels terse and avoid jargon in help text. :sparkles:
